title: S025 — Incremental Phase-A fixpoint equivalence
description: Attempt an actual incremental Phase-A execution: reset the affected dependency closure to NEITHER, then call the authoritative seeded Phase A, and compare against the from-scratch reference at every prefix.
result_summary: BLOCKED. The shadow incremental Phase A (reset the affected dependency closure to NEITHER, then call the authoritative seeded positiveFixpoint via the new phaseATruth) is NOT equivalent to the from-scratch reference: 800 prefixes tested, 152 divergent (19.0%). First divergence: ordos seed=0 prefix=5 iv=negateEvent:ev/vaela-invested, with 3 nodes changed OUTSIDE an 11-node reset closure. ROOT CAUSE (dependency-index / support-loss): the from-scratch Phase A is a sticky LEAST fixpoint over the whole node set, so a support change can re-decide nodes not reverse-reachable from the directly-changed nodes (the S015/S017 result at the Phase-A level); nodes left with a stale prior value are never re-evaluated because the seeded sticky rule skips decided nodes. WHY BLOCKED: the candidate is sound iff the reset set is a superset of the re-decided set; widening to a guaranteed superset means resetting everything = from-scratch propagation. S021's aggregate is exact and is NOT the failure. No second FOUR evaluator, no reimplemented support rule; the only novelty was reset scope. No further rules were added (failure discipline).

answers.root_cause: reset scope: the dependency closure under-approximates the re-decided set
answers.new_semantic_machinery_required: no - but the only sound reset is the whole model = from-scratch
answers.incremental_phase_a_exact: not with the maintained aggregate/dependency state

next_architectural_question: Either prove a sound reset superset bound (if one exists), or accept from-scratch Phase A and pursue the S008/S012 retention boundary instead.
limitations: 800 prefixes (20 histories x H=20 x 2 canons); the first divergence is at prefix 5, adequate to refute the candidate but not a large-scale study.
Only the reset-closure design was tested; other incremental designs (e.g. a non-sticky chaotic iteration with a proven least-fixpoint start) were not attempted.
